correctness.rationale: For p/q reduced and 1<=m,n<q distinct with m+n=q, the first-order q-return forcing sum vanishes by geometric roots-of-unity cancellation. Expanding q iterates to epsilon^2 gives S2=sum_(0<=i<j<q) h_prime(x+jp/q)h(x+ip/q). Its Fourier coefficient at k+l is -2*pi*i*q*k*c_k*c_l/(1-zeta^l) for k+l divisible by q and 0 otherwise. Only frequencies 0 and ±q remain. Algebra yields C0=-(pi*q/2)(m A^2-n B^2)cot(pi*p*m/q) and Cq=(pi*q*A*B/4)[-(n-m)cot(pi*p*m/q)+i q]exp(i(phi+psi)). Therefore nonzero width pi*|AB| sqrt(q^2+(n-m)^2*cot^2)*epsilon^2+O(|epsilon|^3), and stated center shift. Positive q-return derivative in detuning makes endpoint problem an extrema problem for -S2/q; for odd q a signed pair sums to q only when m+n=q. Independent 816 direct Fourier-sum versus coefficient comparisons across reduced rotations and phases gave max relative discrepancy 9.4e-13; a finite test is not the all-parameter proof. Remainder fixed q/amplitudes, no uniform large-q claim.
residual_risks: Finite diagnostics are only corroboration; infinite assertions rest on the reconstructed proof.

value.rationale: The Fourier resonance arithmetic identifies exactly when two distinct low harmonics can generate a quadratic rational locking tongue (for odd denominator), and quantifies its universal strictly positive width with numerator dependence. This is motivated by mode-locking control and includes an exact family classification across infinitely many denominators, rather than just a trivial instance; it neither claims novelty of perturbative normal forms nor broad high-order tongues.
residual_risks: Standard high-order circle-map normal forms may include an equivalent explicit specialization in unindexed literature.
Only q fixed and nonzero fixed amplitudes covered; weak forcing cannot justify higher-order terms for noncomplementary pairs.

limitations: Asymptotic fixed p/q,m,n,A,B,phases; no uniform denominator and no higher-order converse.
Exact coefficient potentially derivable from older normal-form literature not fully exhausted.
